description_short.value: Accra-based pharmaceutical manufacturer making syrups, tablets, creams and other medicines; formed in 2020 from the merger of Dannex, Ayrton Drug Manufacturing and Starwin Products.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Dannex Ayrton Starwin PLC 2024 Annual Report (GSE PR 364/2025: report of the directors, nature of business; operating segments note) and the GSE merger announcement (PR 006/2020)

description_full.value: Dannex Ayrton Starwin PLC manufactures, imports and sells pharmaceutical products. It runs as a single business making syrups, tablets, creams, suspensions, disinfectants, lozenges, powders, capsules and emulsions; syrups brought in about 56% of its GHS 173.1 million revenue in 2024. The company was formed by a court-approved amalgamation of Dannex Plc with two listed drug makers, Ayrton Drug Manufacturing Ltd (formerly Adcock Ingram's Ghanaian subsidiary) and Starwin Products Ltd. Ayrton and Starwin shareholders received one new share for every 3.13 Ayrton or 12.50 Starwin shares, and the merged company's shares began trading on the Ghana Stock Exchange on 15 January 2020. At the end of 2024 Equatorial Cross Acquisitions, wholly owned by the board chairman Nik Amarteifio, held 60.04% of the shares and SSNIT 17.14%. Its registered office is on Dadeban Road in Accra's North Industrial Area. The directors say the Food and Drugs Authority's requirement that all drug makers become fully WHO cGMP compliant will need significant capital spending, and they recommended no dividend for 2024.
